title: 測量学Ⅰ
subtitle: Surveying I
educationalGoal: (1) Students will acquire basic knowledge of surveying laws and operational specifications for public surveys. (2) Students will learn the principles of survey methods such as observation processing, distance surveying, leveling and the uses of basic surveying equipment.(3) Students will become acquainted with spatial information engineering such as GNSS and GIS, which are new surveying techniques that will be learned in Surveying II
advice: (1) Overview: outline of the history of surveying development, spatial information technology and a regional science seminar (Camelia Kids) (2) Surveying acts: laws related to surveying, the revised Survey Act, operational specifications for public surveys, public surveying and geodetic coordinates 2000 (3) Processing of observations: observational error, propagation of errors, calculation methods and error propagation, least squares method, observation processing, observation processing calculations, conversion between radians and degrees (4) Distance surveys: distance survey bases, direct distance surveys, errors in distance surveys, electro-optical distance meters and principles of stadia surveys (5) Leveling: leveling classification, definition of terms, direct leveling, indirect leveling and types of leveling equipment (6) Answer questions relating to national examinations for assistant surveyors on topics 1 to 5 listed above (related to national qualifications recognition). They will conduct self-checks in classrooms and Knowledge Square, facilitated by a senior SA each time. Reference the e-syllabus for the latest information of class relating Covid-19.
requiredKnowledge: This course is indispensable for taking Surveying Practice/Seminar I and II and is useful preparation for Spatial Information Engineering. Surveying Practicum/Exercise I and II present the lecture contents as a specific application. Spreadsheet software(Excel) can be applied to many survey calculations. Students need to be able to submit reports made using spreadsheets.

activityGoals.body: Students can explain the various surveying methods, the principles of spatial information technology.(0.1L)
Students can correctly select survey methods according to the terrain and survey purpose. (0.1L)
Students can deepen their knowledge of spatial information technology and design/planning. (0.1H, 0.1M)
Students can solve basic and applied question from national registered surveyors.(0.1H, 0.1M)
Students can explain the importance of surveying and spatial information technology.(0.1H, 0.1M)
Students can deepen their awareness of regional collaboration by studying the science seminar. (0.1L, 0.1M)

achievementLevels.ideal: Students can explain the Surveying Act and operation specifications for public surveys. They can explain the geodetic coordinates 2000 accurately, particularly the difference between the world geodetic system and the Japanese geodetic system. Students can handle surveying errors by applying basic mathematical knowledge. They can use the least squares method and process observed values. They can explain the relationship between radians and degrees, and can use Excel to create worksheets. They can also explain the concepts of distance measurement and error, can handle errors, understand and explain the leveling method.
achievementLevels.standard: Students know about the Surveying Act and specifications for public surveys. They can outline the geodetic coordinates 2000. They can also use basic mathematical knowledge and can handle survey errors. Students can explain the relationship between radians and degrees, the concepts of and errors in distance surveys, leveling, and can outline 3S technology.

lessons.content: Teacher's introduction. Explanation of course management policy and introduction to the knowledge and applications taught in Surveying I. Students will understand the bases for evaluation such as attendance, report submission, self-reflection exams and achievement confirmation exams. Reference the e-syllabus for the latest information of class relating Covid-19 (From the 2nd to the 15th).
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks. “Ace” hereafter denotes the book Ace Surveying. “Introduction” denotes the book Outline of Spatial Information Technology, and page numbers indicate assigned pages in each. Ace: pp.1-3 Introduction: pp.1-6 Reference the e-syllabus for the latest information of class relating Covid-19 (From the 2nd to the 15th) .
lessons.assignments: Preparation: Investigate related laws at LC. (pp.1-2) Reference the e-syllabus for the latest information of class relating Covid-19 (From the 2nd to the 15th).

lessons.content: Overview of the Survey Act. Outline of Geodetic Coordinates 2000.
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks. Explain surveying laws. Ace: pp. 8-10
lessons.assignments: Review: Understand the contents of PPT. Preparation: Investigate survey-related laws in detail.

lessons.content: Revised Survey Act (1) Contents of surveying work covered by the Surveying Act.
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks. Explanation of reserved books (specifications for public surveys). Ace: pp. 8-10
lessons.assignments: Review: Survey the revised Survey Act from the Homepage of the Geospatial Institute of Japan (GSI). Preparation: Survey the specifications for public surveys. Use reserved books (specifications for public surveys).

lessons.content: Revised Survey Act (2) Acquisition of registered surveyors and assistant surveyors. Specifications for public surveys. (Especially contents to be implemented in the surveying practicum /exercise)
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks. Practice specifications for public surveys. Utilization of reserved books (specifications for public surveys) and active learning
lessons.assignments: Review: Examine differences from the old Surveying Act. Use reserved books (specifications for public surveys) Preparation: Mathematical basis of surveying. Use reserved books(specifications for public surveys) and active learning.

lessons.content: The relationship between the earth and surveying. Mathematical fundamentals. Observational error, propagation of errors, calculation methods and error propagation, least squares method, observation processing, calculations for observation processing, conversion between radians and degrees.
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks Practice significant digits (active learning) Ace: pp. 11-21 Introduction: pp. 7-10, pp.17-47
lessons.assignments: Review: Understand the least squares method and processing of data. pp.15-21 Preparation: Research propagation of errors and the meaning of propagation. pp. 13-15. Prepare overview of Camellia Kids.

lessons.content: General exercises - Movie: "THURUGIDAKE TEN NO KI". The movie schedule is subject to change depending on the progress of the class. Commentary and airing time is about 3 hours.
lessons.operation: Watch a movie Write an impression of the movie.
lessons.assignments: Review: Investigate Yoshitaro Shibasaki of the Army Geodetic Survey Department. Preparation: Take the Web test (Moodle). Consider the theme of the regional collaboration (Camelia Kids).

lessons.content: General exercises - Movie: "THURUGIDAKE TEN NO KI"(Continued from 6th class).
Introduction and practice of distance surveying, a basic survey type. Concepts of distance surveying, direct distance surveying, errors in distance surveying.
lessons.operation: Self -reflection test and practice. Ace: pp.1-21 Group discussion on spatial science seminar.
lessons.assignments: Review: Review chapters 1 and 2 of the text, particularly areas where understanding is weak. Preparation: Prepare for distance surveying.

lessons.content: Introduction and practice of distance surveying, a basic survey type. Concepts of distance surveying, direct distance surveying, errors in distance surveying.
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks. Practice significant digit (active learning) Ace: pp. 21-23 Introduction: pp. 10-12 Explanation of distance measurement.
lessons.assignments: Review: Consider the results of measuring with a measuring tape with errors. (pp. 26-27) Understand indirect surveying. (pp. 28-29) Preparation: Prepare for electro-optical distance meters and stadia surveys.

lessons.content: Continued learning and practice of distance surveying, a basic survey type. Electro-optical distance meters and stadia surveys.
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks. Practice stadia survey (active learning) Ace: pp. 29-33
lessons.assignments: Review: Review the principles of Electro-optical distance meters and stadia surveying. Review indirect surveying. (pp.28-29) Preparation: Prepare for direct leveling.

lessons.content: Introduction and practice of leveling, a basic survey type. Leveling classifications, definition of leveling terminology, direct leveling, level types and tools.
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks. Explanation of direct leveling. Ace: pp. 33-51 Introduction: pp. 56-66
lessons.assignments: Review: Understand technical terms used in leveling. Understand direct leveling. (pp. 33-34) Preparation: Understand leveling classifications (distributed materials and PPT file). Prepare for writing method for field books.

lessons.content: Continued learning and practice of leveling, a basic survey type. Direct leveling, level typesand tools.
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks. Practice direct leveling. (active learning) Ace: pp. 33-51 Introduction: pp. 56-66
lessons.assignments: Review: Understand technical terms used in leveling. Understand direct leveling. (pp. 33-34) Preparation: Prepare for profile leveling and rise-fall leveling. Understanding how to write in a field book.

lessons.content: Procedures for recording leveling data. Profile leveling, rise-fall leveling, level sensitivity, tilting of the staff. Explanation of profile leveling and rise-fall leveling.
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks. Explanation of field book. (active learning) Ace: pp. 33-51 Introduction: pp. 56-66
lessons.assignments: Review: Understand how to write in a field book (pp. 43-46). Review problems that could not be solved. Preparation: Research level sensitivity, tilting of staff.

lessons.content: Procedures for recording leveling data. Level sensitivity, tilting of the staff. Practice profile leveling and rise-fall leveling.
lessons.operation: Lecture, questions and self-checks. Practice field books and level sensitivity. (active learning) Ace: pp. 33-51 Introduction: pp. 56-66
lessons.assignments: Understand how to write in a field book (pp. 43-46). Preparation: Install a 3D simulator on the PC to prepare for Surveying II

lessons.content: Confirmation test: A national examination (registered assistant surveyor) is assumed. Administer student questionnaires.
lessons.assignments: Review: Review of confirmation test. Moodle exam.
